outcome.technical: REDESIGN, as ordered: attribution is now per path, by evidence, and fails closed. audit-task.py: the task-tree release (_tree_resident) is deleted. _held_reading(project, git_root, plan, node, mpath, config, rows=_READ_ROWS) releases a held path only through _own_work_paths, and every exception there releases nothing. A path is released only when ALL of the following hold. (1) _vouching_return finds the starting task's newest executor return that passes every check: it is filed under one of the task's own journaled start keys (_start_keys reads the startedAt changes); _fr.read_filed_return_checked reports no problem and no unchecked note; the filing row is present; the filing moment is at or after the kept snapshot's startedAt; the task was in_progress at the filing (_filed_while_running uses the same journal file's own order, and only the moment across files, where a change in the filing's own second answers False); and its stamp parses with a dirtyPaths map. (2) The path's per-path digest in that stamp equals the digest in _tree_stamp.take(git_root) now. This is the stamp module's own list on both sides, not the whole-tree digest (L1). (3) The path was clean in the task's kept start snapshot (_scoped_commit.read_attempt), which closes writes from before the task began. (4) Every other declarer holding the path was not in_progress at any moment from that start to the filing (_status_events plus _ran_within over the journal's status rows, with inclusive second boundaries). Here None (no events, or a last change that does not match the current status) counts as charged. This closes M1, which the snapshot alone does not: probe_b's P1.1 snapshot was clean. rows=None, meaning an unreadable journal, releases nothing. file-return now refuses an executor return for a task that is not in_progress (H1). _held_dirt_refusal(tid, held, git_root) names `/audit:task unblock <id> --reason '<concrete>'` for blocked holders, or `git -C <root> add -- <paths> && git -C <root> commit -m '<holder>: uncommitted work in <paths>, committed on its own before <tid> starts' -- <paths>`. Everything is shlex-quoted, with no placeholder (M3, L4). The start comment now says that on a restart this is the only check, because record_attempt keeps attempt 1's snapshot (H2 note). commit-task-work.py: predates_remedy is replaced by ways_past(manifest, task, project, git_root, paths, what) plus _declarers. It names the started, unfinished other declarers (unblock for blocked ones, and their id leads the commit message), uses `git -C` the root, and has a concrete message. The MIXED refusal now prints ways past too (M2). verbs-in-full.md describes the four-part evidence rule, the fail-closed list, that a task tree is no evidence, the file-return refusal, and the `git -C` remedy. PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md: `--write-map` diff is still the one `_tree_stamp` token. Tests (lo-block, ae-block): hw1 is a first start over a held change whose holder has a marked task tree; it is refused, nothing is written, and no attempt is spent (probe_a3/M2). hw2 is the same on a restart (probe_a/a2/H2). hw3 ALLOW is the own filed work, with the evidence printed. hw4 is refused for: a return with no filing row (probe_c); a filing row with no digest of the bytes; a foreign start key; a hand filing while pending; and `file-return` on a pending task, which itself gets E_USAGE (probe_c2). hw5 is refused for: bytes moved; the path dirty in the snapshot; the return edited after its row; a snapshot newer than the filing; and journal unread (rows=None) versus read whole. hw6 is the concurrent holder (probe_b/M1). hw7 checks the remedy predicate. hw8 runs the printed commit from <proj>/src: it commits src/a.ts alone, src/b.ts stays dirty, the message names P1.1, and there is no '<'. hw9 checks the predicate both ways. ctw-at11 checks the predicate on the predates refusal; ctw-at12 checks `git -C` with no placeholder; ctw-at13 checks that the MIXED refusal names a guard-passing `git -C` commit; ctw-at14 checks that declarers are named, with done, pending-unattempted and unrelated tasks not named. The fixtures share one journal history and copy it per case. Each order-sensitive step is a second apart (three sleeps of 1.1 s), because rows from different writers order only by second. lo-block runs in about 14 s. Probe re-runs against this fix: probe_a: both starts are refused (exit 2). probe_a2 and probe_a3: start is refused (exit 2), but the probe then runs commit-task-work anyway and it commits src/a.ts. probe_b: restart refused (exit 2); the probe's forced commit-task-work then commits both edits for P1.1. probe_c: refused (2). probe_c2: file-return gets E_USAGE, then start is refused (2). probe_t: remedy verdict about 0.42 s, passing; a path with a space and an apostrophe round-trips through shlex.split. A caller who runs it after a refused start (probe_a2, a3 and b do this on purpose) still commits whatever the kept snapshot reads as `during`. Its own suite's fixtures commit tasks recorded `done`, so a status guard there is a separate decision.
